about.title: About me
body: I am Robin and was born on January 16th 2004 in The Netherlands, Veenendaal, where I currently live.
I've always been fascinated with technology and games and what is possible when using it to help people.
I love working with a driven team on challenging projects, especially ones meant to help people.
Last but not least, let me tell you a bit more about myself outside of being a developer.
My hobbies mainly consist of gaming and playing D&D with my friends with me usually being the DM.
Love making stories for characters and locations.
I always have a bunch of ideas for new stories and love taking inspiration from shows or games while still being original.
In adition to all of that, I also love listening to music.
If you're interested, feel free to listen to my favorite songs.

about: This is a group project from my third year of coding,
and we released it on Itch.io.
Hop 'till you drop is a twin-stick shooter with a cute art style.
Because it was a school project, we had very limited time to work on it,
but even with that time limit I was happy with how it turned out.
If you'd like to play this project, you can click the itch.io button.
Feel free to check out the source code on GitHub as well.
code-1: This code was made to rotate the player either based on the mouse position or the right stick of a controller.
It switches between the two based on which one was used last,
so if you were using the mouse and then switched to the controller it would switch to the right stick and the other way around too.
It makes use of Unity's new input system (which isn't really so new anymore).
I'm happy the way the aiming turned out in the end,
it was a bit tricky to get it working well with both input types, especially switching between the two,
but I think it ended up working pretty well.
code-2: This code was made to let the player pause the game while they play it.
I had a bit of trouble getting the pausing to work well with the shooting mechanics,
as the player could still shoot while the game was paused, which obviously wasn't the intended behavior.
Luckily I saw a way out with use of the game manager and it ended up working well.
In the end I'm happy that it worked once I realised the solution.

about: This is a project from my first year of coding.
Back then I was very inexperienced and didn't have the knowledge I have today, so I decided to rework all of the code.
This was a group project with other developers who were also in their first year of coding.
They made good code for that stage, and I am sure they have improved just like I have.
You can find both the reworked and original code on the GitHub page by switching branches.
